cfo_reading: Deficit-to-surplus swing managed; hold >= 0
what_it_means: What is left of revenue after the year's expenses. No published sector standard; the internal policy floor is breakeven. The FY2023 deficit year and the FY2025 recovery are both visible here.

cfo_reading: Above 1.0x both of the last two years
what_it_means: Revenue divided by expenses - the simplest solvency read. 1.0x means the year paid for itself; below 1.0x the year drew down reserves to operate.

cfo_reading: Share of spending added to net assets - positive again since FY2024
what_it_means: The year's surplus restated as a share of spending - how much the year added to reserves per dollar spent. No published standard; positive years rebuild reserves, negative years draw them down.

cfo_reading: Surplus per dollar of balance sheet - no sector standard
what_it_means: Surplus earned per dollar of total assets. No sector standard for nonprofits - read it as a trend line, not against a benchmark.

benchmark_or_policy: INTERNAL POLICY: >= 3.0 months operating cash (sector norm 3-6)
cfo_reading: THE red flag: cash fell through the 3-month floor in FY2025 as liquidity moved to the portfolio
what_it_means: Pure cash liquidity: Part X cash + savings against a month of spending, excluding the investment portfolio. Internal policy floor is 3.0 months. FY2025 sits far below it because liquidity moved into investments - the board conversation is how fast portfolio assets can become cash.

cfo_reading: Day-count twin of months of cash - 13.9 days vs the ~90-day norm
what_it_means: How many days of spending the unrestricted cash could cover if revenue stopped - the day-count twin of months of cash. Sector guidance is ~90 days (3 months). FY2025 is a fraction of that, so the working question is how quickly portfolio assets can convert to cash.

benchmark_or_policy: SECTOR: 3-6 months reserves; target 6+ when slow-paying reimbursement grants dominate
cfo_reading: Healthy on paper - but line 27 includes fixed assets; get the audit's spendable split
what_it_means: How long the organization could sustain itself on unrestricted net assets if revenue stopped. Sector goal is 3-6 months; target 6+ when slow-paying reimbursement grants dominate. JSV's line 27 includes fixed assets, so the spendable figure is lower than shown.

math_fy2025: (cash 515,092 + savings 0 + pledges receivable 542,806 + AR 5,513 + prepaid 289,681) / (AP 1,182,810 + grants payable 0 + deferred rev 720,632)
cfo_reading: Below 1.0 in FY2025 on the 990 proxy - the balance-sheet echo of the cash story
what_it_means: Short-term assets against short-term bills (990 proxy: cash, savings, receivables and prepaid vs payables, grants payable and deferred revenue). Healthy band is 1.0-2.0. FY2025 dips below 1.0 - the balance-sheet echo of the cash story, softened by the investment portfolio sitting outside the short-term lines.

cfo_reading: Earned fees are the engine (~60% of revenue) - the JCC operating model
what_it_means: Earned program fees as a share of total revenue. High reliance means results track enrollment and utilization - the JCC operating model - and is read next to revenue concentration.

cfo_reading: Donated share of revenue - swings hard with campaigns
what_it_means: Donated dollars as a share of total revenue. Swings with campaign cycles; read together with fundraising efficiency.

cfo_reading: Portfolio and misc income share - small but growing role
what_it_means: Portfolio and miscellaneous income as a share of revenue. Small but growing - earned by the same portfolio that months of cash excludes.

benchmark_or_policy: SECTOR: keep any single revenue stream under 30-40% of total
math_fy2025: program service rev (largest stream) 8,506,012 / total rev 14,208,155
cfo_reading: Above the 30-40% guidance - but the top stream is earned fees from many payers, not one funder
what_it_means: Largest single revenue stream as a share of total revenue - funding-diversity risk. Sector guidance keeps any stream under 30-40%. JSV runs above that, but the top stream is earned program fees from many families, a very different risk than dependence on one grant or donor.

benchmark_or_policy: BENCHMARK: BBB >= 65% on programs; community-center median ~74.2%; above ~90% can signal underinvestment in infrastructure
cfo_reading: Beats the BBB floor and the ~74% sector median every year - a board-ready strength
what_it_means: Share of total spending that goes directly into community programming versus admin and fundraising. Watchdogs (BBB) set a 65% floor; the community-center median is ~74.2%. Centers carry higher facility costs, and above ~90% can signal underinvestment in infrastructure or safety.

benchmark_or_policy: BENCHMARK: <= 35% overhead (complement of the BBB 65% program standard)
cfo_reading: Well under the 35% ceiling
what_it_means: Management & general plus fundraising as a share of total expenses - the watchdog 'overhead' number funders read first. BBB standards imply a 35% ceiling.

benchmark_or_policy: OWNER RULE: management & general < 20% of total expenses
cfo_reading: Admin (M&G) alone stays under the owner's 20% rule
what_it_means: Management & general costs as a share of total expenses - overhead excluding fundraising. The board rule here is under 20%; small or growing organizations legitimately run higher while building infrastructure, so read the trend, not one year.

benchmark_or_policy: SECTOR: personnel typically 45-60% of expenses (upper bound drawn)
cfo_reading: In the 45-60% band since FY2022 (staffed service model)
what_it_means: Salaries, wages and benefits as a share of total expenses. Staff-delivered centers (front desk, instructors, camps) typically run 45-60%; below 45% can mean understaffing, above 60% squeezes program delivery.

cfo_reading: Regranting share of spending - the Federation legacy role
what_it_means: Regranting to other organizations as a share of spending - the Federation legacy role inside the merged organization.

benchmark_or_policy: BENCHMARK: BBB <= 35 cents per contribution $ (sector typical 15-20 cents)
cfo_reading: Cheap fundraising by sector standards
what_it_means: Cents spent on fundraising per contribution dollar raised. BBB ceiling is 35 cents; a typical healthy range is 15-20. JSV raises money cheaply - single digits most years.

benchmark_or_policy: SECTOR: raise $5 or more per $1 spent on fundraising
cfo_reading: Raises ~$8 per $1 spent vs the $5 sector bar
what_it_means: Dollars of contributions raised per dollar of fundraising expense - the flip side of fundraising efficiency. The sector bar is about $5 raised per $1 spent.

cfo_reading: No published standard; strong equity, mostly donor-restricted
what_it_means: Net assets as a share of total assets - how much of the balance sheet the organization owns outright. Strong here, but much of it is donor-restricted or tied up in fixed assets.

cfo_reading: Low reliance on debt (0.27x liabilities to net assets)
what_it_means: Total liabilities against net assets - reliance on debt. 0.27x is low; borrowing capacity exists if the board ever wants it.

benchmark_or_policy: IRS RULE: >= 33 1/3% public support (Schedule A test)
math_fy2025: as filed, Schedule A Part II line 14 - IRS 5-year computation, not recomputed
cfo_reading: IRS 33 1/3% public support test, as filed on Schedule A - passed with 2x headroom every year
what_it_means: The Schedule A public support test as filed: at least one third of support must come from the general public and government over a rolling five years, with any single donor capped at 2% of the base. Falling under 33 1/3% triggers the 10% facts-and-circumstances fallback; sustained failure risks private-foundation reclassification.
